definitions.explanation: The act of removing one thing and putting another in its place. Used for replacing people, items, or contents.
The process of one group leaving and another arriving, such as audiences between shows or employees rotating in shifts.

examples.japanese: {選手|せんしゅ}の{入|い}れ{替|か}えがあった。
{電池|でんち}の{入|い}れ{替|か}えをする。
{衣替|ころもが}えの{季節|きせつ}に、クローゼットの{中身|なかみ}を{入|い}れ{替|か}えた。
examples.english: During the seasonal wardrobe change, I swapped out the contents of the closet.

examples.japanese: {映画館|えいがかん}は{完全|かんぜん}{入|い}れ{替|か}え{制|せい}です。
examples.english: The cinema operates on a complete turnover system.

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}と{夜|よる}でスタッフの{入|い}れ{替|か}えがある。
examples.english: There is a staff changeover between day and night.

examples.japanese: コンサートは{二部|にぶ}{入|い}れ{替|か}え{制|せい}で、{一部|いちぶ}の{客|きゃく}は{退場|たいじょう}しなければならない。
examples.english: The concert has a two-part turnover system, so the first-part audience must leave.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {入|い}れ{替|か}える (to replace, swap). Common in both everyday and business contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入|い}れ{替|か}え{制|せい}: turnover system (audiences must leave between shows)
- {入|い}れ{替|か}え{戦|せん}: relegation/promotion playoff
- {完全|かんぜん}{入|い}れ{替|か}え: complete turnover
- メンバーの{入|い}れ{替|か}え: membership change; roster shake-up

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {交換|こうかん}: exchange — mutual giving and receiving between two parties
- {交代|こうたい}: rotation — taking turns in a role or position
- {差|さ}し{替|か}え: replacement — substituting one item for another, often documents or components
